  - Typed SDK errors instead of text/template's strings, with the engine's
    leak-prone diagnostic kept out of the wire-safe half.
  - Eager parsing AND an escaping probe at construction, so a broken tree is
    a deploy that does not come up rather than a 500 on the one page nobody
    smoke-tested.
  - A byte ceiling, because text/template's Execute takes no context and
    cannot be cancelled.

# Read this before calling TrustHTML

[TrustHTML] is the one place escaping can be bypassed, and it is the only
spelling the SDK offers for it. Six of html/template's seven trust types —
CSS, HTMLAttr, JS, JSStr, URL and Srcset — are REFUSED when they appear in
render data, with the path that carries them named in the error.

What that buys is precise, and the limit is worth reading twice:
[TrustedHTML] is a type ALIAS of html/template.HTML, because html/template
recognises its trust types by an exact type switch and a distinct type would
simply be escaped like any other string. The engine therefore CANNOT tell a
fragment marked through [TrustHTML] from one a caller converted directly.

So the SDK does not prevent a bad trust decision — it cannot see one. What
it prevents is an ACCIDENTAL one, and what it provides is a single greppable
word for the deliberate one. Every call is an assertion that the string was
produced by the server and sanitised. It is never correct to hand it a
string that arrived from a request, from a user-controlled database field,
or from a third-party API.

# Rendering is all-or-nothing

[Renderer].Render returns a []byte. It does not take an io.Writer, and that
is what the port is shaped by: template execution writes incrementally and
can fail halfway, so handed an http.ResponseWriter it would have flushed the
status line, the headers and a plausible prefix of the page before reporting
the failure — at which point 500 is no longer sendable and the browser
renders a truncated document. The engine renders into a bounded buffer it
owns and hands back the complete bytes or nothing at all.

# Parse once. This is the one performance rule the domain has.

Build the [Renderer] at start-up and keep it. It is immutable after
construction, safe for concurrent use, and holds no writer, no file and no
stream. Constructing one per request re-parses the whole tree and re-runs
the escaping analysis on every request; measured on a forty-two-template
tree, that is 34 times the time and 34 times the bytes of reusing one, and
the ratio grows with the tree — see internal/service/app/view/BENCH.md.
There is deliberately no reload, no lazy parse and no cache, because each of
them would put a mutex on the read path to solve a problem that a package
variable already solves.

# Scope

The SDK ships the extension point and one implementation of it. It does not
ship a template LANGUAGE: layouts, block inheritance, helper libraries,
in-template i18n and asset pipelines are framework opinions. Template
composition is whatever the engine's own syntax already provides — for
html/template that is {{define}} and {{template}}, which this package
neither extends nor conventionalises.

symbols.name: Action
symbols.doc: Action is what one command does — see [Command].

symbols.name: AmbiguousCommand

code.public: A command may declare an action or sub-commands, not both

symbols.doc:
AmbiguousCommand refuses a command carrying BOTH an Action and
sub-commands, where adding a child would silently change what an
existing command line means.

symbols.name: Binder
symbols.doc: Binder declares one command's flags onto the stdlib set that parses them.

symbols.name: Command
symbols.doc:
Command is one declared command: a name, what it says about itself, its
flags, and EITHER an [Action] OR sub-commands.

symbols.name: CommandPanicked

code.public: The command panicked and was recovered

symbols.doc:
CommandPanicked is returned when an [Action] panicked. The recovered
value and the originating stack travel as fields; the status stays
EX_SOFTWARE (70).

symbols.name: Config
symbols.doc: Config configures [New] — two writers, and deliberately nothing else.

symbols.name: DuplicateCommand

code.public: Two sub-commands are declared under the same name

symbols.doc: DuplicateCommand refuses two sub-commands of one group sharing a name.

symbols.name: Execute
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, cfg Config, root Command, args []string) error
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, cfg github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/cli.Config, root github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/cli.Command, args []string) error
symbols.doc:
Execute is the one-line form of [New] followed by [Executor].Execute. It
returns the same errors both would: a construction refusal carries EX_CONFIG
(78), so a caller that only wants a status can pass the result straight to
[Status].

symbols.name: Executor
symbols.doc: Executor resolves an argument vector against a command tree and runs it.

symbols.name: FlagSource
symbols.doc:
FlagSource turns the flags an operator ACTUALLY TYPED on one invocation into
a config layer, for use as the LAST source of a config.Load or
config.LoadSchema — the position that makes a flag win over a file and over
the environment.

It walks flag.FlagSet.Visit and never VisitAll: an unset flag contributes
NOTHING, so a flag whose default is the Go zero cannot silently override the
configuration file on every run. The flag name is the config key verbatim,
with no case or separator transformation, because a rename rule is a second
grammar whose failure mode is a key that quietly matches nothing.

symbols.name: FlagSourceValue
symbols.doc: FlagSourceValue is one invocation's typed flags as a config layer.

symbols.name: HelpWriteFailed

code.public: The help could not be written

symbols.doc:
HelpWriteFailed is returned when -h asked for the help and the stream it
goes to did not take the page — a closed pipe, a full disk. The
stream's own error stays matchable beneath it, or rides in a field when
it is itself an SDK error, so the code and EX_IOERR (74) are always this
one's. A bad command line keeps its EX_USAGE even when its help could
not be written.

symbols.name: InvalidCommand

code.public: The command declaration is not runnable and was refused

symbols.doc:
InvalidCommand refuses a declaration that could never be reached or
could never run: a blank name, a name that would be parsed as a flag, a
child with no summary, or neither an Action nor sub-commands.

symbols.name: InvalidFlags

code.public: The flags for this command could not be parsed

symbols.doc:
InvalidFlags is returned when package flag refused the vector. EX_USAGE
(64).

symbols.name: Invocation
symbols.doc: Invocation is one resolved command line as an [Action] sees it.

symbols.name: MissingCommand

code.public: This command needs a sub-command

symbols.doc:
MissingCommand is returned when a group is invoked with no sub-command.
EX_USAGE (64).

symbols.name: New
symbols.spelled: func(cfg Config, root Command) (runner Executor, err error)
symbols.doc:
New validates a whole command tree and returns the [Executor] that runs it.

The WHOLE tree is checked, not the branch an invocation happens to take, so
a mis-wired `tool db migrate` fails on the first run of the binary rather
than on the first run of the migration. Every refusal carries EX_CONFIG
(78).

Each [Binder] is CALLED once here, on a throwaway flag set, which is what
proves it binds no reserved name — so a Binder must be safe to call more
than once and must touch only the set it is given.

symbols.name: ReservedFlag

code.public: The flag names -h and -help are answered by the SDK

symbols.doc:
ReservedFlag refuses a Binder that bound -h or -help, the two names the
SDK answers itself.

symbols.name: Status
symbols.doc:
Status is the process exit status for what [Executor].Execute returned: 0
when err is nil, and errs.ExitCodeOf(err) otherwise.

It is a guard on the SDK's existing convention and not a second one.
errs.ExitCodeOf answers "what status does THIS ERROR map to", so it returns
the EX_SOFTWARE default (70) for a nil it was never meant to be handed —
which is correct for an accessor and catastrophic at a CLI boundary, where
success is the common case. This is the one place in the SDK where nil has
to mean 0, so this is where the guard lives.

	os.Exit(cli.Status(app.Execute(ctx, os.Args[1:])))

symbols.name: Success
symbols.doc: Success is the process exit status of a command that did what it was asked.

symbols.name: UnknownCommand

code.public: That sub-command does not exist

symbols.doc:
UnknownCommand is returned when a token names no sub-command of the
group it was typed under. EX_USAGE (64).

symbols.name: DecodeFailed

symbols.doc: DecodeFailed is returned when the merged config cannot decode into the target.

symbols.name: EnvSource
symbols.doc:
EnvSource returns a Source reading "PREFIX_KEY" env vars (empty prefix = all).

The key a field must match is the variable name with the prefix removed and
lower-cased, underscores kept: under EnvSource("APP"), the variable
APP_SDM_SERVER_NAME feeds a field tagged `json:"sdm_server_name"`. The
separating underscore belongs to the Source, and a trailing one on prefix is
absorbed, so EnvSource("APP") and EnvSource("APP_") name the same namespace.

A value is coerced to a typed Go value only when the WHOLE value is one
complete JSON document — "8080" becomes an int64, "true" a bool. Anything
else keeps its exact string, so identifiers that merely start like numbers
("0A0A01", "1500ms", "10.45.0.0/16", "2026-09-03") arrive intact.

An EMPTY prefix reads the whole process environment, so pairing it with a
schema that refuses unknown keys refuses PATH, HOME and everything else the
shell exported. That is a fact about the source, not about the schema: give
the source a prefix, or set [SchemaSpec].AllowUnknownKeys.

called, never replaced.

of its keys, so one restart tells the whole truth. A nil schema is refused by
name rather than silently loading nothing.

symbols.name: EventType

EventType is the public alias for the concrete Go type a subscription is
keyed on. It is reflect.Type; [On] and [Off] derive it for you.

symbols.name: Halt

code.public: A listener stopped the event dispatch

symbols.doc:
Halt is the control sentinel a listener returns to stop the dispatch.
Only a listener registered with MayHalt may use it.

symbols.name: HaltNotPermitted

code.public: A listener tried to stop the dispatch without the authority to

symbols.doc:
HaltNotPermitted reports a Halt from a listener without MayHalt. The
dispatch continued.

symbols.name: Handler
symbols.doc: Handler is the public alias for one TYPED listener's registration.

symbols.name: InvalidEventType

symbols.doc: InvalidEventType refuses a type no dispatch could ever match.

symbols.name: InvalidSubscription

code.public: The event subscription is not runnable and was refused

symbols.doc: InvalidSubscription refuses a registration with no name or no listener.

symbols.name: Listener
symbols.doc:
Listener is the public alias for the ERASED reaction the bus dispatches.
Most code never names it — [On] builds one from a typed function.

symbols.name: ListenerFailed

code.public: An event listener reported an error

symbols.doc:
ListenerFailed is the bus's verdict on a listener that returned an
error; it travels beside that error, never around it.

symbols.name: ListenerPanicked

code.public: The event listener panicked and was recovered

symbols.doc: ListenerPanicked reports a recovered listener panic.

symbols.name: New
symbols.doc:
New returns an empty in-process event bus. It cannot fail and takes no
configuration: every knob considered was a contract rather than a setting,
and a bus whose semantics vary by construction cannot be read at the call
site.

symbols.name: Off
symbols.spelled: func[E any](bus Bus, name string) error
symbols.doc:
Off removes the listener registered under name for the event type E. A name
that is not registered is [UnknownListener], never a silent success.

symbols.name: On
symbols.spelled: func[E any](bus Bus, handler Handler[E]) error
symbols.doc:
On registers a typed listener for the event type E.

It is a function rather than a method because Go methods cannot take type
parameters — and a Bus[E] would carry exactly one event type, which is a
channel and not a bus.

E must be a concrete type; an interface is refused with [InvalidEventType].

symbols.name: Priority
symbols.doc:
Priority is the public alias for a listener's position in the dispatch
order. Lower runs first.

symbols.name: PriorityNormal
symbols.doc:
PriorityNormal is the zero Priority: negative values run before it,
positive values after.

symbols.name: Subscription
symbols.doc:
Subscription is the public alias for one ERASED registration. Prefer
[Handler] with [On]; this is the shape a caller who has already erased the
type themselves registers.

symbols.name: UnknownListener

code.public: No listener is registered under that name for this event

symbols.doc: UnknownListener reports an Unsubscribe naming nobody.

symbols.name: Ask
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, cfg AskConfig) (status int, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, cfg github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/health.AskConfig) (status int, err error)
symbols.doc:
Ask asks the process listening on cfg.Addr whether it is ready: one GET of
cfg.Path over plain HTTP, the question a container's HEALTHCHECK asks. It
returns the status the process answered — zero when no whole answer, body
included, arrived within the bound — and a nil error exactly when that
status is 200; otherwise the error is
AskMisconfigured, AskUnreachable, AskTimeout or AskNotReady. See the package
documentation for what the exchange refuses to do.

symbols.name: AskConfig
symbols.doc:
AskConfig is the public alias for where a process listens and which path
answers whether it is ready: Addr and Path are required, Timeout and Clock
have working zeros.

symbols.name: AskMisconfigured

code.public: The readiness probe was given an address, path or timeout it cannot use

symbols.doc:
AskMisconfigured refuses an Ask no answer could satisfy — an address
with no usable port, a path that is not absolute, a negative timeout —
before anything is dialled. The "argument" field names which.

symbols.name: AskNotReady

code.public: The process answered that it is not ready

symbols.doc:
AskNotReady reports an Ask the process answered with a status other
than 200 — a redirect included, since none is followed. The "status"
field carries it; the body never does.

symbols.name: AskTimeout

code.public: The process did not answer the readiness probe in time

symbols.doc:
AskTimeout reports an Ask with no answer when its budget, or the
caller's context, ended. A caller's own context error stays in the
chain, so errors.Is answers context.Canceled or DeadlineExceeded too.

symbols.name: AskUnreachable

code.public: The process could not be reached

symbols.doc:
AskUnreachable reports an Ask the process never answered because the
connection or the request failed; the transport's error is the cause.

symbols.name: Check
symbols.doc:
Check is the public alias for the ctx-aware body of a startup or readiness
check. It is the shape a dependency call has.

symbols.name: CheckFailed

code.public: A health check reported a failure

symbols.doc:
CheckFailed is the identity a PLAIN error from a check is given. An
error that already carries an SDK Code keeps its own.

symbols.name: CheckPanicked

code.public: The health check panicked and was recovered

symbols.doc:
CheckPanicked is the failure of a check whose body panicked. It was
recovered; the panic value travels as a field and never reaches a body.

symbols.name: CheckTimeout

code.public: A health check did not answer within its budget

symbols.doc:
CheckTimeout reports a check that had not answered when its budget
expired. A failure, not an unknown — Result.TimedOut is what
distinguishes it.

symbols.name: Component
symbols.doc:
Component adapts a registry to pkg/v1/app/lifecycle: its Start runs the startup
checks, its Stop marks the process draining. The returned value IS a
lifecycle.Component.

Add it LAST — see the package documentation for why one rule covers both
directions.

symbols.name: Config
symbols.doc: Config is the public alias for the registry's construction parameters.

symbols.name: DefaultAskTimeout
symbols.doc:
DefaultAskTimeout is the budget an Ask gets when AskConfig.Timeout is
zero: three seconds, an order of magnitude under Docker's own
HEALTHCHECK timeout, so a probe that gets no answer says why first.

symbols.name: DefaultCheckTimeout
symbols.doc:
DefaultCheckTimeout is the per-check budget a non-positive Timeout
clamps to.

symbols.name: Draining

code.public: The process is shutting down and is no longer accepting traffic

symbols.doc:
Draining is the synthetic result of a readiness probe answered after
Drain. No readiness check was run, and no later probe will say anything
else.

symbols.name: DuplicateCheck

code.public: A health check is already registered under that name

symbols.doc:
DuplicateCheck is returned by an Add whose name is already registered
on that probe. The namespace is per probe, so the same name may appear
once on readiness and once on liveness.

symbols.name: HandlerConfig
symbols.doc: HandlerConfig is the public alias for a handler's body verbosity.

symbols.name: Health
symbols.doc: Health is the public alias for the registry contract.

symbols.name: InvalidCheck

code.public: The health check is not runnable and was refused

symbols.doc:
InvalidCheck is returned by every Add for a check that could never run
— an empty Name or a nil Check. The "missing" field names which.

symbols.name: LivenessCheck
symbols.doc:
LivenessCheck is the public alias for process-local evidence that the
process is not irrecoverable.

symbols.name: MaxAskDrainBytes
symbols.doc:
MaxAskDrainBytes is how much of a response body Ask reads before it
closes the connection: enough for any readiness answer to end politely,
and a bound on one that never ends.

symbols.name: MaxCacheAge
symbols.doc:
MaxCacheAge is the ceiling on ReadinessCheck.MaxAge. Above it, a
registration is refused rather than clamped.

symbols.name: New
symbols.doc:
New returns a Health. It cannot fail: a nil cfg.Clock falls back to the wall
clock, a non-positive cfg.DefaultTimeout to DefaultCheckTimeout, and nil
hooks to no observation. What can fail fails at registration.

symbols.name: NewLivenessHandler
symbols.doc:
NewLivenessHandler serves the liveness probe: 200 unless the process is
irrecoverable. Nothing outside the process can make it return 503, because
nothing outside the process can be registered on it.

symbols.name: NewReadinessHandler
symbols.doc:
NewReadinessHandler serves the readiness probe: 200 while the replica can
take traffic (healthy OR degraded), 503 otherwise — including while starting
and after Drain.

symbols.name: NewStartupHandler
symbols.doc:
NewStartupHandler serves the startup probe: 200 once every startup check has
passed, 503 while any has not.

symbols.name: NotifyFailed

code.public: The readiness notification could not be delivered

symbols.doc:
NotifyFailed reaches Config.OnNotifyError when an opt-in sd_notify
datagram could not be delivered.

symbols.name: Probe
symbols.doc: Probe is the public alias for which of the three questions is being asked.

symbols.name: ProbeLiveness
symbols.doc: ProbeLiveness asks "is this process irrecoverable?".

symbols.name: ProbeReadiness
symbols.doc: ProbeReadiness asks "can this replica take traffic right now?".

symbols.name: ProbeStartup
symbols.doc: ProbeStartup asks "is this process still coming up?".

symbols.name: ReadinessCheck
symbols.doc:
ReadinessCheck is the public alias for a check that gates routing. Every
dependency check belongs here.

symbols.name: Report
symbols.doc: Report is the public alias for one probe's whole answer.

symbols.name: Result
symbols.doc: Result is the public alias for one check's answer.

symbols.name: SelfCheck
symbols.doc:
SelfCheck is the public alias for the body of a LIVENESS check. It takes no
context, which is what keeps a dependency call out of the probe that
restarts the process.

symbols.name: StaleCacheWindow

code.public: The health check cache window is longer than the SDK will vouch for

symbols.doc:
StaleCacheWindow is returned by AddReadiness for a MaxAge above
MaxCacheAge.

symbols.name: StartupCheck
symbols.doc: StartupCheck is the public alias for a check that gates startup.

symbols.name: StartupPending

code.public: The process is still starting and is not accepting traffic yet

symbols.doc:
StartupPending is the synthetic result of a readiness probe answered
while the process is still starting. No readiness check was run.

symbols.name: Status
symbols.doc: Status is the public alias for a check's or a probe's verdict.

symbols.name: StatusDegraded
symbols.doc:
StatusDegraded is a failing NON-critical check. It is a serving state:
the handler returns 200.

symbols.name: StatusHealthy
symbols.doc:
StatusHealthy is every check passing — including a probe with no checks
registered at all.

symbols.name: StatusUnhealthy
symbols.doc:
StatusUnhealthy is a failing critical check, or a probe with one. It is
the ZERO value of Status on purpose: a forgotten assignment must read
as "not serving", never as "everything is fine".

symbols.name: UnknownProbe

code.public: The requested health probe does not exist

symbols.doc:
UnknownProbe is carried by a report for a Probe value the SDK never
mints, including the zero value.

symbols.name: Worst
symbols.doc:
Worst returns the more severe of two statuses — the SDK's whole aggregation
rule, exported so a caller composing several registries applies the same one.

symbols.name: Args
symbols.doc:
Args binds placeholder names to the text that replaces them. It is
map[string]string on purpose — see the package comment.

symbols.name: ArgumentMissing

code.public: A placeholder the message names was not supplied

symbols.doc:
ArgumentMissing is returned when [Args] does not carry a placeholder
the pattern names. It names the placeholder and never a value.

symbols.name: Catalog
symbols.doc:
Catalog is the message-source port, frozen at two methods (ADR 0039).
[Store] implements it.

symbols.name: CatalogInvalid

code.public: The message catalogue is not usable and was refused

symbols.doc:
CatalogInvalid is returned for a catalogue that cannot be compiled: an
unset or unserved fallback, a duplicate tag, or an entry of the wrong
shape.

symbols.name: CatalogLoadFailed

code.public: The message catalogue could not be read or decoded

symbols.doc:
CatalogLoadFailed is returned when a catalogue directory cannot be read
or its bytes cannot be decoded. The cause stays in the chain, so
errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) still answers.

symbols.name: Catalogue
symbols.doc: Catalogue is one language's entries, keyed by message key.

symbols.name: Count
symbols.doc:
Count is a quantity described by the CLDR plural operands. It carries the
DISPLAY precision, because a quantity of one shown with a decimal is a different category
in English and a float64 cannot tell them apart.

symbols.name: Decimal
symbols.spelled: func(value float64, fractionDigits int) (count Count, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(value float64, fractionDigits int) (count github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/i18n.Count, err error)
symbols.doc:
Decimal returns the [Count] of value displayed with exactly fractionDigits
fraction digits, or [InvalidCount].

The second argument is the DISPLAY precision, not a property of the value:
Decimal(1, 2) describes "1.00", which is `other` in English, while
[Int](1) describes "1", which is `one`.

symbols.name: Entry
symbols.doc:
Entry is one catalogue entry before it is compiled: a plain pattern
([Plain]) or one pattern per CLDR category ([PluralForms]).

symbols.name: Fallbacker
symbols.doc:
Fallbacker is the ADR 0039 sibling that names a catalog's fallback language.
A catalog with no fallback does not implement it, and the absence is the
answer.

symbols.name: Form
symbols.doc:
Form is a CLDR plural category. [FormOther] is the zero value, because it is
the only category every language defines.

symbols.name: FormFew
symbols.doc: FormFew is the small plural of the Slavic and Semitic families.

symbols.name: FormMany
symbols.doc:
FormMany is the large plural, and the compact-decimal form in several
Romance languages.

symbols.name: FormOne
symbols.doc: FormOne is the singular of languages that have one.

symbols.name: FormOther
symbols.doc:
FormOther is the catch-all. Every language defines it and every message must
carry it.

symbols.name: FormTwo
symbols.doc: FormTwo is the dual.

symbols.name: FormZero
symbols.doc: FormZero is the distinct nought of Arabic and Latvian.

symbols.name: Int
symbols.doc:
Int returns the [Count] of an exact integer displayed with no fraction
digits. The sign is discarded, because CLDR's operands are defined on the
absolute value.

symbols.name: InvalidCount

code.public: The quantity cannot be described by CLDR plural operands

symbols.doc:
InvalidCount is returned by [Decimal] for a NaN, an infinity, or a
fraction-digit count outside 0..9.

symbols.name: InvalidForm

code.public: The plural category name is not one of the six CLDR defines

symbols.doc:
InvalidForm is returned by [ParseForm] for a name outside the six CLDR
categories.

symbols.name: InvalidKey

code.public: The message key is empty or contains a control character

symbols.doc:
InvalidKey is returned for an empty message key, or one carrying a
control character.

symbols.name: InvalidPattern

code.public: The message pattern is malformed and was refused

symbols.doc:
InvalidPattern is returned for a malformed pattern: an unclosed brace,
an unmatched closing brace, or a placeholder name outside
[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*.

symbols.name: InvalidTag

code.public: The language tag is not one this SDK resolves

symbols.doc:
InvalidTag is returned by [ParseTag] for a tag outside the
`language[-Script][-REGION]` subset. It is NOT what a peculiar
Accept-Language header produces: [Negotiator].Negotiate skips an
element it cannot use and never fails.

symbols.name: Key
symbols.doc:
Key names a message inside a catalogue. It is a developer identifier —
"checkout.button.pay" — and it is what a render puts on screen when the
translation is missing.

symbols.name: KeyLister
symbols.doc:
KeyLister is the ADR 0039 sibling that enumerates a catalog's keys, reached
by type assertion. [Store].Missing is what it exists for.

symbols.name: LoadFS
symbols.spelled: func(fsys fs.FS, dir string, format codec.Format, fallback Tag) (store *Store, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(fsys io/fs.FS, dir string, format github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/codec.Format, fallback github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/i18n.Tag) (store *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/i18n.Store, err error)
symbols.doc:
LoadFS reads one catalogue file per language from dir and returns a [Store].

The bytes are decoded by the codec domain, so a catalogue is JSON, YAML,
TOML or any other registered format and this package contains no parser —
blank-import pkg/v1/data/codec to register one. fsys is io/fs.FS, so an embed.FS,
an os.DirFS and a pkg/v1/data/vfs filesystem all work here unchanged.

The language comes from the file NAME: "en.json", "pt-PT.yaml".
Subdirectories are ignored rather than walked, and two files that
canonicalise to one tag are [CatalogInvalid].

symbols.name: Message
symbols.doc:
Message is one compiled translation. Its placeholders are parsed when the
catalogue is built, so a malformed pattern fails at startup and a render
never parses.

symbols.name: MessageNotFound

code.public: No translation exists for this message key

symbols.doc:
MessageNotFound is returned when no language in the chain holds the
key. The render still returns a non-empty string — the key itself.

symbols.name: NegotiationEmpty

code.public: Language negotiation was set up with no supported languages

symbols.doc:
NegotiationEmpty is returned by [NewNegotiator] for an empty supported
set, which is an unfinished wiring rather than "accept anything".

symbols.name: Negotiator
symbols.doc:
Negotiator resolves an Accept-Language header to one of a fixed set of
languages. Everything that can be wrong is refused when it is built, so
[Negotiator].Negotiate has no failure mode.

symbols.name: NewMessage
symbols.doc: NewMessage compiles an uncounted message, or returns [InvalidPattern].

symbols.name: NewNegotiator
symbols.doc:
NewNegotiator returns a [Negotiator] over supported, falling back to
fallback, or refuses: an empty supported set is [NegotiationEmpty], an unset
or unsupported fallback is [CatalogInvalid].

symbols.name: NewPluralMessage
symbols.doc:
NewPluralMessage compiles a counted message from one pattern per category,
or returns [InvalidPattern], [InvalidForm] or [PluralFormMissing]. The map
MUST contain [FormOther].

It does not check the map against any language's rules — it does not know
the language. [NewStore] does, and refuses there.

symbols.name: NewPrinter
symbols.spelled: func(catalog Catalog, tag Tag) (printer *Printer, err error)
symbols.doc:
NewPrinter returns a [Printer] rendering tag out of catalog, or refuses.

It resolves the chain and allocates; [Printer].Render walks it and does not.
Build one per language at startup and index them by [Tag] — a request then
costs a map lookup, not a construction.

symbols.name: NewStore
symbols.spelled: func(fallback Tag, catalogues map[Tag]Catalogue) (store *Store, err error)
symbols.doc:
NewStore compiles catalogues into a [Store], or refuses.

Every check is here, and every failure is a startup failure:
[UnsupportedLanguage] for a language with no reviewed rule,
[TranslationIncomplete] for a counted message missing one of its language's
categories, [CatalogInvalid] for an unset or unserved fallback, and the core
refusals for a bad key, pattern or category name.

symbols.name: ParseForm
symbols.doc:
ParseForm returns the [Form] named by a CLDR category spelling — "zero",
"one", "two", "few", "many", "other" — or [InvalidForm].

symbols.name: ParseTag
symbols.doc:
ParseTag canonicalises text into a [Tag], or returns [InvalidTag].

"FR-latn-ca" and "fr-Latn-CA" are the same Tag. The POSIX spelling
("fr_FR"), extensions, variants, private use and grandfathered tags are each
refused by name rather than parsed and dropped — a dropped subtag changes
which language answers without changing anything a reader can see.

symbols.name: Plain
symbols.doc: Plain returns an uncounted [Entry].

symbols.name: Plural
symbols.doc:
Plural is one language's CLDR plural specification: the categories it can
produce, and the rule that picks between them.

symbols.name: PluralFormMissing

code.public: The message does not carry the plural form this quantity requires

symbols.doc:
PluralFormMissing is returned when a message is asked for a category it
does not carry. A catalogue built by [NewStore] cannot produce it.

symbols.name: PluralForms
symbols.doc:
PluralForms returns a counted [Entry] whose patterns are keyed by CLDR
category name. A counted entry is checked at load against every category its
language can produce.

symbols.name: PluralRule
symbols.doc:
PluralRule reports which CLDR category a quantity falls in for one language.
It is a func type, which satisfies ADR 0039 structurally.

symbols.name: Printer
symbols.doc:
Printer renders messages in one language. Build one per language at startup,
not one per request — see [NewPrinter].

symbols.name: Rules
symbols.doc:
Rules returns the CLDR plural specification for tag, and reports whether the
SDK has one. It resolves the exact tag first and the bare language second,
so "pt-PT" gets its own rule and "fr-CA" inherits French's.

symbols.name: Store
symbols.doc:
Store is the concrete, immutable catalogue. It implements [Catalog],
[KeyLister] and [Fallbacker].

symbols.name: SupportedTags
symbols.doc:
SupportedTags returns every language this SDK has a reviewed CLDR plural
rule for, sorted. It is what [UnsupportedLanguage] names beside a refused
tag.

symbols.name: Tag
symbols.doc:
Tag is a language, optionally narrowed by a script and a region:
`language[-Script][-REGION]` and deliberately nothing else. It is
comparable, so it is a map key, and it holds its canonical spelling, so
[Tag].String allocates nothing.

symbols.name: TranslationIncomplete

code.public: A plural message is missing a form its language requires

symbols.doc:
TranslationIncomplete is returned for a counted message missing a
category its language can produce — the one catalogue defect a
translator cannot see by reading their own file.

symbols.name: UnsupportedLanguage

code.public: No reviewed plural rule exists for this language

symbols.doc:
UnsupportedLanguage is returned when a catalogue or a printer names a
language this SDK has no reviewed CLDR plural rule for. It is the
domain's central refusal — see the package comment.

symbols.name: ValidateKey
symbols.doc:
ValidateKey reports whether key is usable, and returns [InvalidKey] when it
is not: empty, or carrying a control character.

symbols.name: Available
symbols.doc: Available returns the sorted list of registered Schemes.

symbols.name: ClockBackwards

code.public: Identifier generation observed the clock moving backwards

symbols.doc: ClockBackwards is returned when a snowflake observes a backwards clock.

symbols.name: EntropyFailed

code.public: Identifier generation failed to read secure random bytes

symbols.doc:
EntropyFailed is kept for code that matches it: nothing returns it since
Go 1.24, whose crypto/rand.Read never fails.

symbols.name: FormatTypeID
symbols.spelled: func(prefix string, uuid string) (typeID string, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(prefix string, uuid string) (typeID string, err error)
symbols.doc:
FormatTypeID renders prefix and a canonical dashed-hex UUID as a TypeID. It
is the migration path: an existing UUID column becomes typed without
reissuing anything, so the UUID version is not enforced.

symbols.name: Generator
symbols.doc: Generator is the public alias for the identifier-generator contract.

symbols.name: InvalidPrefix

code.public: Identifier generation requires a valid lowercase type prefix

symbols.doc:
InvalidPrefix is returned by NewTypeID, ParseTypeID and FormatTypeID for a
type prefix that is empty or outside lowercase ASCII.

symbols.name: InvalidSize

code.public: Identifier generation requires a positive identifier length

symbols.doc: InvalidSize is returned by NewNanoID for a non-positive identifier length.

symbols.name: KSUID
symbols.doc:
KSUID returns a fresh KSUID: 27 base62 characters that sort by creation time
as plain strings. Feed the result to ParseKSUID to recover that time.

symbols.name: KSUIDScheme
symbols.doc: KSUIDScheme is the KSUID scheme key.

symbols.name: Malformed

code.public: The identifier is not well formed for its scheme

symbols.doc:
Malformed is returned by ParseKSUID, ParseTypeID and FormatTypeID when the
input is not a well-formed rendering for its scheme.

symbols.name: NanoID
symbols.doc:
NanoID returns a fresh 21-character NanoID over the URL-safe alphabet. The
characters are drawn by rejection sampling, so every symbol is equally
likely; 21 of them carry 126 bits, slightly more than a UUIDv4.

symbols.name: NanoIDScheme
symbols.doc: NanoIDScheme is the NanoID scheme key.

symbols.name: New
symbols.doc: New generates a fresh identifier using the generator registered under scheme.

symbols.name: NewNanoID
symbols.doc:
NewNanoID returns a NanoID Generator producing size characters, and refuses a
non-positive size rather than return one that mints empty strings. Not added
to the global registry — the registered NanoID singleton is the 21-character
default.

symbols.name: NewSnowflake
symbols.doc:
NewSnowflake returns a snowflake Generator bound to an explicit node id
(reduced into the 10-bit node space). Not added to the global registry.

symbols.name: NewTypeID
symbols.doc:
NewTypeID returns a TypeID Generator stamping prefix on every identifier —
"user_01h2xcejqtf2nbrexx3vqjhp41". prefix must be 1 to 63 lowercase ASCII
letters, with '_' allowed only between two letters; anything else is refused
here rather than at every call. Not added to the global registry, because no
prefix would be a defensible default (see TypeIDScheme).

symbols.name: ParseKSUID
symbols.spelled: func(ksuid string) (issued time.Time, payload [16]byte, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(ksuid string) (issued time.Time, payload [16]byte, err error)
symbols.doc:
ParseKSUID decodes a canonical 27-character KSUID, returning the instant it
was issued (second resolution, UTC) and its 16-byte random payload.

symbols.name: ParseTypeID
symbols.spelled: func(typeID string) (prefix string, uuid string, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(typeID string) (prefix string, uuid string, err error)
symbols.doc:
ParseTypeID splits a canonical TypeID into its type prefix and the dashed-hex
UUID its suffix encodes. It is the exact inverse of FormatTypeID.

symbols.name: Scheme
symbols.doc: Scheme is the public alias for the identifier-scheme key.

symbols.name: Snowflake
symbols.doc: Snowflake returns a fresh id from the default-node snowflake generator.

symbols.name: SnowflakeScheme
symbols.doc: SnowflakeScheme is the snowflake scheme key.

symbols.name: TimestampRange

code.public: Identifier generation observed a clock outside the scheme's timestamp range

symbols.doc:
TimestampRange is returned when the clock sits outside the window a
scheme's timestamp field can represent.

symbols.name: TypeIDScheme
symbols.doc:
TypeIDScheme is the TypeID scheme key. It is the only scheme key New
cannot resolve: a TypeID needs a type prefix, and there is no
non-arbitrary prefix the SDK could choose on a caller's behalf, so no
generator is registered under it. New(TypeIDScheme) returns
UnknownScheme by design — build one with NewTypeID instead. The key is
exported because Generator.Scheme() reports it.

symbols.name: ULID
symbols.doc: ULID returns a fresh ULID (26-char Crockford base32, lexically time-sortable).

symbols.name: ULIDScheme
symbols.doc: ULIDScheme is the ULID scheme key.

symbols.name: UUIDv4
symbols.doc: UUIDv4 returns a fresh random UUIDv4 in canonical dashed-hex form.

symbols.name: UUIDv4Scheme
symbols.doc: UUIDv4Scheme is the random-UUID scheme key.

symbols.name: UUIDv7
symbols.doc: UUIDv7 returns a fresh time-ordered UUIDv7 (k-sortable by creation time).

symbols.name: UUIDv7Scheme
symbols.doc: UUIDv7Scheme is the time-ordered UUID scheme key.

symbols.name: UnknownScheme

code.public: No identifier generator is registered under that scheme

symbols.doc:
UnknownScheme is returned by New when no generator is registered under the
requested Scheme. Matchable via errs.HasReason(err, "UNKNOWN_SCHEME").

symbols.name: Component
symbols.doc: Component is the public alias for one named Start/Stop registration.

symbols.name: ComponentPanicked

code.public: The lifecycle component panicked and was recovered

symbols.doc:
ComponentPanicked is the failure of a component whose Start or Stop
panicked. It was recovered; the panic value travels as a field.

symbols.name: Config
symbols.doc: Config is the public alias for the engine's construction parameters.

symbols.name: DefaultHealthyRun
symbols.doc:
DefaultHealthyRun is how long a supervised run must last, when
SupervisorConfig.HealthyAfter is not positive, for its end to count as
a first failure again.

symbols.name: DefaultRestartBase
symbols.doc:
DefaultRestartBase is the supervisor's first restart backoff when
SupervisorConfig.Backoff is zero, or sets no BaseDelay; it doubles from
there.

symbols.name: DefaultRestartMax
symbols.doc:
DefaultRestartMax is the supervisor's longest restart backoff when
SupervisorConfig.Backoff is zero.

symbols.name: DefaultStopTimeout
symbols.doc:
DefaultStopTimeout is the per-component budget a non-positive
Config.StopTimeout clamps to.

symbols.name: DuplicateComponent

code.public: A component is already registered under that name

symbols.doc: DuplicateComponent is returned by Add when the name is already taken.

symbols.name: InvalidComponent

code.public: The lifecycle component is not runnable and was refused

symbols.doc:
InvalidComponent is returned by Add for a component that could never
run — an empty Name, a nil Start, a nil Stop. The "missing" field names
which.

symbols.name: Lifecycle
symbols.doc: Lifecycle is the public alias for the ordered start/stop contract.

symbols.name: LifecycleRunning

code.public: The lifecycle is already started

symbols.doc:
LifecycleRunning is returned by Add, and by a second Start, while the
Lifecycle is started. Add before Start, or after Stop returns.

symbols.name: New
symbols.doc:
New returns a Lifecycle. It cannot fail: a nil cfg.Clock falls back to the
wall clock, a non-positive cfg.StopTimeout to DefaultStopTimeout, and a nil
cfg.OnTransition to no observation. What can fail fails at Add.

symbols.name: NewSupervisor
symbols.spelled: func(name string, run func(ctx context.Context) error, cfg SupervisorConfig) (*Supervisor, error)
symbols.canonical: func(name string, run func(ctx context.Context) error, cfg github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/lifecycle.SupervisorConfig) (*github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/lifecycle.Supervisor, error)
symbols.doc:
NewSupervisor builds a supervisor named name over run, tuned by cfg — whose
zero value is a working supervisor. run must return when its context ends;
returning earlier, or panicking, restarts it after the backoff. It starts
nothing: Start does, or the Lifecycle it is a Component of.

symbols.name: Phase
symbols.doc:
Phase is the public alias for which half of a component a Transition
reports.

symbols.name: PhaseStart
symbols.doc: PhaseStart reports a call to a component's Start.

symbols.name: PhaseStop
symbols.doc: PhaseStop reports a call to a component's Stop.

symbols.name: ReadinessFailed

code.public: The readiness notification could not be delivered

symbols.doc:
ReadinessFailed is returned when an opt-in sd_notify datagram could not
be delivered.

symbols.name: Run
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, lc Lifecycle, cfg RunConfig) error
symbols.doc:
Run starts every component, waits for ctx or one of cfg.Signals, then stops
them in reverse order. See the package documentation for what the opt-in
fields wire, and what the zero RunConfig deliberately does not.

symbols.name: RunConfig
symbols.doc: RunConfig is the public alias for Run's opt-in supervision wiring.

symbols.name: RunPanicked

code.public: The supervised function panicked and was recovered

symbols.doc:
RunPanicked is the failure of a supervised run that panicked. It was
recovered and the run restarted; the panic value and the stack travel
as fields, never in the Public text.

symbols.name: Signal
symbols.doc:
Signal is the public alias for a typed OS signal, re-exported here so a
caller wiring RunConfig.Signals needs no second import.

symbols.name: Start
symbols.doc: Start is the public alias for the ctx-aware bring-up half of a component.

symbols.name: StartFailed

code.public: A component failed to start and the started components were stopped

symbols.doc:
StartFailed is joined with the component's own error when a Start
aborts the sequence. The components already up were stopped first.

symbols.name: Stop
symbols.doc: Stop is the public alias for the ctx-aware teardown half of a component.

symbols.name: StopFailed

code.public: A component reported an error while stopping

symbols.doc:
StopFailed is joined with the component's own error when its Stop
returns one. The shutdown continued with the remaining components.

symbols.name: StopTimeout

code.public: A component did not stop within its budget and was abandoned

symbols.doc:
StopTimeout reports a component whose Stop had not returned when its
budget expired. Its context was cancelled and it was abandoned — never
killed, and nothing it owns was closed on its behalf.

symbols.name: SupervisionEvent
symbols.doc:
SupervisionEvent is the public alias for one thing a supervisor did, as
its observer is told.

symbols.name: SupervisionPhase
symbols.doc: SupervisionPhase is the public alias for what a SupervisionEvent reports.

symbols.name: SupervisionRestarting
symbols.doc: SupervisionRestarting reports a restart scheduled after Delay.

symbols.name: SupervisionRunEnded
symbols.doc: SupervisionRunEnded reports a run returning, or panicking.

symbols.name: SupervisionRunStarted
symbols.doc: SupervisionRunStarted reports a run of the supervised function beginning.

symbols.name: SupervisionStopped
symbols.doc: SupervisionStopped reports the end of the supervision.

symbols.name: Supervisor
symbols.doc:
Supervisor is the public alias for a function run until stopped and
restarted after every early end: Start, Stop, Component.

symbols.name: SupervisorConfig
symbols.doc:
SupervisorConfig is the public alias for a supervisor's optional tuning:
Clock, Observe, Backoff, HealthyAfter.

symbols.name: SupervisorMisconfigured

code.public: The supervisor cannot run as configured

symbols.doc:
SupervisorMisconfigured refuses a supervisor without a name or a
function.

symbols.name: SupervisorRunning

code.public: The supervisor is already running

symbols.doc: SupervisorRunning refuses a second Start while a supervision runs.

symbols.name: Transition
symbols.doc: Transition is the public alias for one reported component move.

symbols.name: UnwindFailed

code.public: Cleaning up after a failed start did not complete cleanly

symbols.doc:
UnwindFailed marks a failure DURING the cleanup of a partial start. It
travels alongside the start failure, never instead of it.

symbols.name: Deadliner
symbols.doc:
Deadliner is the sibling implemented by a [Lease] that CAN expire — i.e. one
that can be taken from you while you are still running.

Its presence is the only question that changes how a caller must be written.
A memory lease implements it; a file lease does not, because a file lock has
no deadline at all. It is deliberately not a Deadline method on [Lease]
returning a zero time for "never": a zero time.Time is a value someone will
compare against time.Now and lose to, and an absent interface is not.

symbols.name: FileConfig
symbols.doc: FileConfig parameterises [NewFileLocker]. Dir must be set; Poll defaults.

symbols.name: Keepalive
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, lease Lease, cfg KeepaliveConfig) (guarded context.Context, stop context.CancelFunc, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, lease github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/lock.Lease, cfg github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/lock.KeepaliveConfig) (guarded context.Context, stop context.CancelFunc, err error)
symbols.doc:
Keepalive renews lease in the background and returns a context that is
CANCELLED the instant the lease stops being held, plus the function that
ends the renewal.

The loss arrives as a cancellation because [Lease].Extend returning an error
only helps a caller currently calling it — and the caller that needs the
news is the one already inside the critical section. context.Cause names it.

	guarded, stop, err := lock.Keepalive(ctx, lease, lock.KeepaliveConfig{Every: ttl / 3})
	if err != nil { return err }
	defer stop()
	// hand `guarded` to the protected work; it ends if the lease is lost

stop does NOT release the lease: the lifetime of a lock must not depend on
the lifetime of a convenience.

symbols.name: KeepaliveConfig
symbols.doc:
KeepaliveConfig parameterises [Keepalive]. Every must be positive and should
be comfortably shorter than the lease TTL — a third of it leaves room for
two consecutive failed renewals.

symbols.name: Lease
symbols.doc:
Lease is a held lock: Fence, Extend, Release. FROZEN at three, for the same
reason [Locker] is frozen at two.

symbols.name: LockBackendFailed

code.public: The lock backend could not serve the operation

symbols.doc:
LockBackendFailed is returned when the locker could not serve the
operation at all. A lock merely being HELD is not this — TryAcquire
reports that as (nil, false, nil).

symbols.name: LockDirectoryUnsafe

code.public: The lock directory's permissions do not protect the lock files

symbols.doc:
LockDirectoryUnsafe is returned by [NewFileLocker] for a world-writable,
non-sticky directory, whose lock files any account could replace with a
fresh inode — splitting one lock into two.

symbols.name: LockFenceCorrupt

code.public: The lock's fencing ledger is not readable

symbols.doc:
LockFenceCorrupt is returned by the file locker when no further token
can be issued from the on-disk fencing ledger — it is not a decimal
counter, or it is the one counter with no successor. Nothing is
repaired: a restarted counter, or a wrapped one, reissues numbers the
protected resource has already accepted.

symbols.name: LockFileReplaced

code.public: The lock file is no longer the file its name leads to

symbols.doc:
LockFileReplaced is returned by Acquire, and by a held lease's Extend,
when the lock file is no longer the file its name leads to: the entry
was unlinked, or replaced, while it was held.

It is the one exposure here that is DETECTED rather than prevented. In
a world-writable sticky directory — /tmp's mode, which the directory
rule accepts by name — the account that created the lock file owns that
entry and may unlink it, including while you hold the lock. Your
descriptor keeps working, because a descriptor outlives its name, and
the next process creates a different file and locks that instead.

When Extend returns it, you are inside a section you no longer own.
Stop the protected work; re-acquiring would give you a second lease
over the new file while the old one is still locked. The prevention is
a lock directory no other account can write, which is what
[NewFileLocker] creates when the directory is absent.

symbols.name: LockKeepaliveLost

code.public: The lease could not be renewed and is no longer held

symbols.doc:
LockKeepaliveLost is the context CAUSE published by [Keepalive] when a
renewal fails.

symbols.name: LockMisconfigured

code.public: The lock cannot be built from the given configuration

symbols.doc:
LockMisconfigured is returned by a constructor whose configuration
cannot be honoured — most importantly a TTL that is not positive.

symbols.name: LockNameRejected

code.public: The lock name is not usable as given

symbols.doc: LockNameRejected is returned for an empty or unusable lock name.

symbols.name: LockNotHeld

code.public: The lease is no longer held by this caller

symbols.doc:
LockNotHeld is returned by Extend or Release when this caller's lease
has been taken over. From Extend it means you are inside a section
someone else owns; stop the protected work.

symbols.name: LockPathRedirected

code.public: The lock path is a link rather than a file

symbols.doc:
LockPathRedirected is returned by [NewFileLocker] when the lock path is
an indirection rather than a file — a symbolic link on Unix, a reparse
point on Windows. The lock and its fencing ledger would land on a file
chosen by whoever planted it, so two processes would hold "the same"
lock over different inodes with nothing reported on either side.

symbols.name: Locker
symbols.doc:
Locker hands out named, exclusive leases: Acquire and TryAcquire.

The method set is FROZEN at two. New capabilities arrive as SIBLING
interfaces you reach by type assertion, because this alias publishes the
interface, Go interfaces are structural, and a third method would break
every downstream implementer at compile time with no deprecation window
(ADR 0039).

symbols.name: MemoryConfig
symbols.doc: MemoryConfig parameterises [NewMemory]. TTL must be positive.

symbols.name: NewFileLocker
symbols.doc:
NewFileLocker returns a [Locker] that excludes every process using the same
directory on the same machine, and whose leases do NOT expire.

It refuses at construction: a missing directory setting, a negative poll
interval, a lock directory any account could put an entry into, and a
platform with no file-range lock at all, where it returns the SDK-wide
UnsupportedPlatform rather than a locker that would report success and
exclude nothing (ADR 0018). Windows is no longer in that last set: it is
served by LockFileEx (ADR 0081).

The third refusal is one rule with two vocabularies, because the two
platforms answer "who can replace an entry here" differently. On Unix it is
a mode: world-writable without the sticky bit. On Windows it is the
directory's DACL: an entry letting Everyone (S-1-1-0), Authenticated Users
(S-1-5-11) or BUILTIN\Users (S-1-5-32-545) unlink somebody else's entry, or
write the lock files the directory will create (ADR 0084, ADR 0086).

Creating an entry at a free name is NOT that right, on either platform: it
is what the sticky bit permits, and what Windows spells as "may add a file"
without "may delete a child". What it costs is a lock file planted before
any holder exists, which is a denial of service rather than a lost
exclusion.

symbols.name: NewMemory
symbols.doc:
NewMemory returns a [Locker] whose leases live in this process and DO
expire.

cfg.TTL must be positive; a zero or negative TTL is refused here rather than
defaulted, because the two natural readings of zero are opposites and either
choice would be silently wrong for half of its callers (ADR 0031).

symbols.name: Address
symbols.doc: Address is the public alias for one RFC 5322 mailbox.

symbols.name: Attachment
symbols.doc:
Attachment is the public alias for one file or inline part. A non-empty
ContentID makes it inline.

symbols.name: AuthFailed

code.public: The mail server rejected the credentials

symbols.doc:
AuthFailed is returned when the server rejected the credentials or
advertised no AUTH mechanism.

symbols.name: AuthInsecure

code.public: Credentials cannot be sent over an unencrypted mail session

symbols.doc:
AuthInsecure is returned when credentials would have travelled over an
unencrypted session — at construction, and again before AUTH.

symbols.name: BatchSender
symbols.doc:
BatchSender is the public alias for the sibling that sends several messages
over one session.

symbols.name: Compose
symbols.doc:
Compose renders msg to the RFC 5322 wire form using the system clock and
crypto/rand. It is the one-line form of [NewComposer].

symbols.name: ComposeFailed

code.public: The message could not be assembled into a MIME body

symbols.doc: ComposeFailed is returned when the MIME body could not be assembled.

symbols.name: Composer
symbols.doc:
Composer is the public alias for the type that turns a [Message] into
the RFC 5322 wire form without sending anything.

symbols.name: ComposerConfig
symbols.doc:
ComposerConfig is the public alias for the composer's optional clock and
randomness source. Both clamp rather than refuse.

symbols.name: DefaultCaptureKeep
symbols.doc:
DefaultCaptureKeep is how many deliveries NewCapture keeps when given a
non-positive number.

symbols.name: Delivery
symbols.doc:
Delivery is the public alias for one record of what a transport put on the
wire: the envelope, and the composed bytes.

symbols.name: DialFailed

code.public: The mail server could not be reached

symbols.doc:
DialFailed is returned when the server could not be reached, or the
context ended before the greeting.

symbols.name: EmptyBody

code.public: A message must carry text, HTML or an attachment

symbols.doc:
EmptyBody is returned for a message with no text, no HTML and no
attachment.

symbols.name: Envelope
symbols.doc:
Envelope is the public alias for the SMTP envelope: one MAIL FROM and every
RCPT TO, Bcc included.

symbols.name: EnvelopeOf
symbols.doc:
EnvelopeOf validates msg and derives the SMTP envelope a transport would
issue for it: the From addr-spec as the return path, and every recipient —
To, then Cc, then Bcc — as a RCPT TO. A blind recipient reaches the envelope
and no header; that is the whole of Bcc in this package.

It returns the first typed refusal [Validate] would, and the zero [Envelope]
with it: an envelope built from an unvalidated message is a list of strings
that may each carry a CRLF.

symbols.name: FullTransport
symbols.doc:
FullTransport is the public alias for the union [NewMemory] returns. A
parameter should still ask for the narrowest thing it uses.

symbols.name: GreetingFailed

code.public: The mail server did not accept the SMTP conversation

symbols.doc:
GreetingFailed is returned when the connection opened and the SMTP
conversation did not.

symbols.name: HeaderField
symbols.doc:
HeaderField is the public alias for one additional header. It is a slice
element rather than a map entry so a composed message is deterministic and so
a field may legitimately repeat.

symbols.name: HeaderInjection

code.public: A message header contains a line break and was refused

symbols.doc:
HeaderInjection is returned when a header name or value carries CR, LF or
NUL. It is a refusal and never a repair, and it names the field rather
than the value.

symbols.name: HeaderTooLong

code.public: A message header is too long to fold and was refused

symbols.doc:
HeaderTooLong is returned when a header line exceeds the RFC 5322 §2.1.1
limit of 998 octets and offers no whitespace to fold at. It is refused
rather than truncated.

symbols.name: InvalidAddress

code.public: A mail address in that message is not usable

symbols.doc:
InvalidAddress is returned for an addr-spec outside the dot-atom subset
of RFC 5322 §3.4.1 this domain accepts, or outside the RFC 5321 §4.5.3.1
length limits.

symbols.name: InvalidAttachment

code.public: An attachment on that message is not usable

symbols.doc:
InvalidAttachment is returned for an attachment with no filename, an
unparseable media type, a malformed Content-ID, or an inline part in a
message with no body to reference it.

symbols.name: InvalidConfig

code.public: The SMTP transport configuration is not usable as written

symbols.doc:
InvalidConfig is returned by [NewSMTP] for a configuration that cannot be
honoured as written — including a [TLSUnset] mode.

symbols.name: InvalidURL

code.public: The SMTP URL is not usable as written

symbols.doc:
InvalidURL is returned by [ParseURL] for a URL it cannot read. It names
the clause and never the URL, which carries the password.

symbols.name: Message
symbols.doc: Message is the public alias for one mail, as a value.

symbols.name: MissingSender

code.public: A message must name the mailbox it is from

symbols.doc: MissingSender is returned for a message with no From mailbox.

symbols.name: NewCapture
symbols.doc:
NewCapture returns NewMemory's double keeping only the last keep deliveries
— DefaultCaptureKeep when keep is not positive: the transport a development
server and a test deliver through.

symbols.name: NewComposer
symbols.doc:
NewComposer returns a composer that renders a [Message] to the RFC 5322 wire form
without sending it — for a caller that hands the bytes to something this SDK
does not implement, or that wants a golden test over its own templates.

A [ComposerConfig] with a fixed clock and a fixed randomness source makes
composition byte-deterministic.

symbols.name: NewMemory
symbols.doc:
NewMemory returns a transport that composes every message and records the
result instead of dialling anything — the double a consumer's tests wire in
place of [NewSMTP].

It takes no arguments on purpose: every knob it could offer is one a test has
to set before it can assert anything, and the value of a double is that it
costs one line.

symbols.name: NewSMTP
symbols.doc:
NewSMTP returns a transport that delivers over SMTP, refusing at construction
any configuration it could not honour — an unset TLS mode, an out-of-range
port, or credentials it would have to send in the clear.

It holds no pooled connection: it dials per send, and a caller that wants one
session for many messages asks for it through [BatchSender].

symbols.name: NoRecipients

code.public: A message must name at least one recipient

symbols.doc:
NoRecipients is returned when To, Cc and Bcc are all empty, before any
socket is opened.

symbols.name: Outbox
symbols.doc:
Outbox is the public alias for the sibling that exposes what was sent. Only
the in-memory transport implements it.

symbols.name: ParseURL
symbols.doc:
ParseURL reads smtp://user:password@host:port?tls=starttls|implicit|none, or
smtps://…, into an [SMTPConfig] that [NewSMTP] accepts; see the package
documentation for the grammar and its defaults. On a refusal it returns the
zero SMTPConfig and an error that never quotes the URL.

symbols.name: ReservedHeader

code.public: That header is set by the mail composer and cannot be overridden

symbols.doc:
ReservedHeader is returned when Headers names a field the composer owns —
including Bcc, which is the injection arriving through the front door.

symbols.name: SMTPConfig
symbols.doc: SMTPConfig is the public alias for the SMTP transport's configuration.

symbols.name: SendRefused

code.public: The mail server refused the message

symbols.doc:
SendRefused is returned when MAIL, RCPT or DATA was answered with a
failure reply. The server's own text travels as a log-only field.

symbols.name: TLSDisabled
symbols.doc:
TLSDisabled sends in the clear and must be spelled out loud. Credentials are
refused with it, at construction.

symbols.name: TLSFailed

code.public: The connection to the mail server could not be encrypted

symbols.doc: TLSFailed is returned when the handshake or the STARTTLS command failed.

symbols.name: TLSImplicit
symbols.doc:
TLSImplicit negotiates TLS before the greeting, which RFC 8314 §3.3 prefers
because there is no plaintext phase to interfere with. The port-465 shape.

symbols.name: TLSMode
symbols.doc: TLSMode is the public alias for the encryption mode. Its zero value is refused.

symbols.name: TLSRequired

code.public: The mail server did not offer the encryption this transport requires

symbols.doc:
TLSRequired is returned when STARTTLS was required and the server never
offered it. The session is ended, never downgraded.

symbols.name: TLSStartTLS
symbols.doc:
TLSStartTLS requires the server to advertise STARTTLS (RFC 3207) and refuses
the session when it does not. The port-587 shape.

There is deliberately no opportunistic variant: a transport that encrypts
when the server offers it and continues in the clear when it does not is one
stripped EHLO line away from handing an attacker the whole session.

symbols.name: TLSUnset
symbols.doc:
TLSUnset is the zero value and is refused at construction — neither
"encrypt" nor "do not" is a guess this SDK is entitled to make for a caller.

symbols.name: Transport
symbols.doc:
Transport is the public alias for the frozen port. A new capability arrives
as a sibling interface reached by type assertion, never as a second method
(ADR 0039).

symbols.name: UnsupportedAddress

code.public: That address form is not supported by this mail transport

symbols.doc:
UnsupportedAddress is returned for a non-ASCII addr-spec (RFC 6531
SMTPUTF8) or a quoted local part — both legal mail, both refused by name
rather than transliterated into a deliverable but different address.

symbols.name: Validate
symbols.doc:
Validate reports whether msg can be composed and sent, returning the first
typed refusal it finds.

It is exported so a caller can reject a message at the edge — where a form
was submitted — rather than at the transport, and get the same verdict either
way.

symbols.name: Attempt
symbols.doc:
Attempt is the public alias for what one delivery attempt knows about
itself, carried in the context the spool hands its transport.

symbols.name: AttemptFrom
symbols.doc:
AttemptFrom returns the attempt a delivery context carries — only a context
a Spool handed its transport carries one.

symbols.name: Closed

code.public: The mail spool is closed

symbols.doc: Closed refuses a Send or a SendWithID after Close.

symbols.name: Config
symbols.doc:
Config is the public alias for a spool's configuration: Transport and
MaxAttempts required; Dir or Broker and Deferrer, Clock, From, Backoff,
SendTimeout, MaxMessageBytes, PollInterval, Observe, Annotate and NewID
optional.

symbols.name: DeadLetter
symbols.doc: DeadLetter is the public alias for a mail the spool gave up on.

symbols.name: DefaultMaxMessageBytes
symbols.doc:
DefaultMaxMessageBytes bounds one spooled mail when
Config.MaxMessageBytes is zero.

symbols.name: DefaultRetryBase
symbols.doc:
DefaultRetryBase and DefaultRetryMax bound the wait between attempts
when Config.Backoff is zero; DefaultRetryBase is also the first wait of
a curve that sets no BaseDelay.

symbols.name: DefaultRetryMax
symbols.doc: The spool's defaults, and its bound on an identifier.

symbols.name: DefaultSendTimeout
symbols.doc:
DefaultSendTimeout bounds one delivery attempt when Config.SendTimeout
is not positive.

symbols.name: DeliveredMemory
symbols.doc:
DeliveredMemory is how many delivered mails a spool remembers to drop a
redelivery.

symbols.name: Event
symbols.doc: Event is the public alias for one thing that happened to one mail.

symbols.name: EventDeadLettered
symbols.doc: EventDeadLettered: the last attempt failed; the mail is kept with it.

symbols.name: EventDuplicate
symbols.doc: EventDuplicate: a redelivery of a mail already delivered was dropped.

symbols.name: EventKind
symbols.doc: EventKind is the public alias for what an Event reports.

symbols.name: EventQueued
symbols.doc: EventQueued: Send put the mail in the spool.

symbols.name: EventRetrying
symbols.doc: EventRetrying: an attempt failed and the next is due at Next.

symbols.name: EventSent
symbols.doc: EventSent: the transport accepted the mail.

symbols.name: InvalidMailID

code.public: The mail identifier is malformed

symbols.doc:
InvalidMailID refuses an identifier Spool.SendWithID was given that is
empty, longer than MaxIDBytes or not an RFC 5322 dot-atom. It names the
rule broken and never the identifier.

symbols.name: MaxIDBytes
symbols.doc:
MaxIDBytes bounds a spooled mail's identifier, whoever minted it:
Spool.SendWithID refuses a longer one with InvalidMailID.

symbols.name: MessageUndecodable

code.public: A spooled mail could not be read back

symbols.doc: MessageUndecodable reports a spooled record that is not a mail.

symbols.name: MessageUnencodable

code.public: The mail could not be written to the spool

symbols.doc: MessageUnencodable refuses a mail Send could not write.

symbols.name: Misconfigured

code.public: The mail spool cannot run as configured

symbols.doc:
Misconfigured refuses a spool that could never deliver, and a Send
whose Config.NewID minted an identifier no mail can keep.

symbols.name: New
symbols.doc:
New builds a durable outbox over cfg.Transport: over cfg.Broker, a queue in
cfg.Dir, or in memory without either. It starts nothing: Run delivers.

symbols.name: Spool
symbols.doc:
Spool is the public alias for the durable outbox: Send, SendWithID, Run,
DeadLetters, Close.

symbols.name: TransportPanicked

code.public: The mail transport panicked and was recovered

symbols.doc:
TransportPanicked is the failure of an attempt whose transport
panicked.

symbols.name: Backoff
symbols.doc:
Backoff is the public alias for the exponential backoff curve NewRetry waits
between attempts, for a loop that backs off on its own terms.

symbols.name: BreakerConfig
symbols.doc: BreakerConfig is the public alias for the circuit-breaker configuration.

symbols.name: BulkheadFull

code.public: The call was rejected because the bulkhead is full

symbols.doc:
BulkheadFull is returned when every concurrency slot is occupied. It
carries HTTP 503.

symbols.name: CircuitOpen

code.public: The circuit breaker is open; the call was rejected

symbols.doc:
CircuitOpen is returned when the breaker rejects a call fast. It carries
HTTP 503 (errs.HTTPStatusOf): the dependency cannot take the call now.

symbols.name: FallbackConfig
symbols.doc: FallbackConfig is the public alias for the fallback policy configuration.

symbols.name: FallbackFailed

code.public: The operation and its fallback both failed

symbols.doc:
FallbackFailed is returned when the primary operation AND its fallback
both failed. Both messages travel as the "primary" and "fallback"
fields, so neither half of a double failure is lost and neither can
hijack the policy's own code.

symbols.name: HedgeConfig
symbols.doc: HedgeConfig is the public alias for the hedging policy configuration.

symbols.name: KeyedRateLimiterConfig
symbols.doc:
KeyedRateLimiterConfig is the public alias for the keyed rate-limiter
configuration: a token bucket per key, bounded in number and forgotten when
idle.

symbols.name: NewBulkhead
symbols.doc: NewBulkhead returns a bounded-concurrency Runner (reject mode).

symbols.name: NewCircuitBreaker
symbols.doc:
NewCircuitBreaker returns a circuit-breaker Runner. An error rejected by
cfg.Retryable is returned verbatim and left out of the state machine.

symbols.name: NewFallback
symbols.doc:
NewFallback returns a Runner that runs cfg.Fallback when the guarded
Operation fails, reporting success when it works. When both fail the result
is FallbackFailed, carrying both messages — unless the context was cancelled,
which is reported as ctx.Err(). A nil cfg.Fallback is refused.

symbols.name: NewHedge
symbols.doc:
NewHedge returns a tail-latency Runner that DUPLICATES an Operation still
outstanding after cfg.Delay and takes the first success. Correct only on an
idempotent Operation, which cfg.Idempotent makes the caller assert: that
field, cfg.Delay and cfg.MaxInFlight are all refused when unset (ADR 0031).

Each copy runs on a goroutine of its own, so a panic in one is recovered
there and re-raised by Run on the caller's goroutine with the ORIGINAL value
— a recover comparing against http.ErrAbortHandler still matches — but with
the stack of the re-raise site; the copy's own stack is the price of not
ending the process. A losing copy's late panic is recovered and dropped.

symbols.name: NewKeyedRateLimiter
symbols.doc:
NewKeyedRateLimiter returns a Runner holding one token bucket per key — the
key cfg.Key names for each call's context — so a caller who empties its
bucket is refused while every other caller is not. At most cfg.MaxKeys keys
are held, the least recently used forgotten first, and a key unused for
cfg.IdleTimeout is forgotten too; a forgotten key starts over with a full
bucket. A non-finite or non-positive cfg.Rate, a nil cfg.Key and a
non-positive cfg.MaxKeys or cfg.IdleTimeout are each refused: every call
returns PolicyMisconfigured, naming the field.

symbols.name: NewRateLimiter
symbols.doc:
NewRateLimiter returns a token-bucket rate-limiter Runner. A non-positive
cfg.Rate is refused: every call returns PolicyMisconfigured without running
the operation, because any rate chosen for the caller would be a guess.

symbols.name: NewRetry
symbols.doc:
NewRetry returns a retry-with-backoff Runner. An error rejected by
cfg.Retryable ends the loop at once and is returned verbatim.

symbols.name: NewTimeout
symbols.doc:
NewTimeout returns a deadline-enforcing Runner. A non-positive d is refused:
every call returns PolicyMisconfigured without running the operation, since
any deadline chosen for the caller would be a guess (ADR 0031).

symbols.name: Operation
symbols.doc: Operation is the public alias for the ctx-aware unit of guarded work.

symbols.name: PolicyMisconfigured

code.public: The reliability policy was misconfigured and refused the call

symbols.doc:
PolicyMisconfigured is returned by every call to a policy that was built
with a configuration it cannot honour — a non-positive RateLimiterConfig
.Rate, a non-positive NewTimeout duration, a nil FallbackConfig.Fallback,
an unasserted HedgeConfig.Idempotent, a non-positive HedgeConfig.Delay or
MaxInFlight, a KeyedRateLimiterConfig without a Key, a MaxKeys or an
IdleTimeout. The operation is not run. Unlike the sentinels above it is
permanent, not transient: the fix is at the construction site, never a
retry (ADR 0031).

symbols.name: RateLimited

code.public: The call was rejected by the rate limiter

symbols.doc:
RateLimited is returned when no rate-limit token is available. It
carries HTTP 429: the client should slow down.

symbols.name: RateLimiterConfig
symbols.doc: RateLimiterConfig is the public alias for the rate-limiter configuration.

symbols.name: RetryConfig
symbols.doc: RetryConfig is the public alias for the retry policy configuration.

symbols.name: RetryExhausted

code.public: The operation failed after exhausting all retries

symbols.doc: RetryExhausted is returned when the retry budget is spent.

symbols.name: Runner
symbols.doc: Runner is the public alias for the composable policy-executor contract.

symbols.name: TimeoutExceeded

code.public: The operation exceeded its timeout

symbols.doc:
TimeoutExceeded is returned when an operation outruns its deadline. It
carries HTTP 504: the call was made and its answer did not arrive in
time.

symbols.name: Config
symbols.doc: Config is the public alias for the engine's construction parameters.

symbols.name: DuplicateJob

code.public: A job is already registered under that name

symbols.doc: DuplicateJob is returned by Add when the name is already registered.

symbols.name: Entry
symbols.doc: Entry is the public alias for one named Schedule/Job registration.

symbols.name: Every
symbols.doc:
Every returns a Schedule due one period after each previous due instant. A
non-positive period is refused. It is deliberately not spelled "@every":
an interval is not a calendar expression.

symbols.name: InvalidEntry

code.public: The scheduler entry is not runnable and was refused

symbols.doc:
InvalidEntry is returned by Add for an entry that could never run — an
empty Name, a nil Schedule, a nil Job. The "missing" field names which.

symbols.name: InvalidExpression

code.public: The cron expression is not valid

symbols.doc:
InvalidExpression is returned by Parse for a malformed or out-of-range
cron field.

symbols.name: InvalidInterval

code.public: The interval must be greater than zero

symbols.doc: InvalidInterval is returned by Every for a non-positive period.

symbols.name: InvalidLocation

code.public: A time zone is required and none was given

symbols.doc: InvalidLocation is returned by ParseInLocation for a nil location.

symbols.name: Job
symbols.doc: Job is the public alias for the ctx-aware unit of scheduled work.

symbols.name: JobPanicked

code.public: The scheduled job panicked and was recovered

symbols.doc:
JobPanicked is the Result.Err of a job that panicked. The scheduler
recovered it and kept running; the panic value travels as a field.

symbols.name: New
symbols.doc:
New returns a Scheduler. It cannot fail: a nil cfg.Clock falls back to the
wall clock and a nil cfg.OnResult to no observation, both of which are
working configurations. What can fail fails at Add and at Parse.

symbols.name: Parse
symbols.doc:
Parse compiles a five-field POSIX cron expression, evaluated in UTC. See the
package documentation for the accepted subset and for what is refused.

symbols.name: ParseInLocation
symbols.spelled: func(expr string, loc *time.Location) (schedule Schedule, err error)
symbols.doc:
ParseInLocation compiles a cron expression evaluated in loc. A nil loc is
refused rather than read as UTC; use Parse to ask for UTC.

symbols.name: Result
symbols.doc: Result is the public alias for one reported scheduling decision.

symbols.name: Schedule
symbols.doc: Schedule is the public alias for the "when is this next due" port.

symbols.name: Scheduler
symbols.doc: Scheduler is the public alias for the engine contract.

symbols.name: SchedulerRunning

code.public: The scheduler is already running

symbols.doc:
SchedulerRunning is returned by Add, and by a second Run, while a Run is
in progress. The entry set is frozen for the duration of a Run; add
before it starts or after it returns.

symbols.name: UnreachableSchedule

code.public: The cron expression matches no date on the calendar

symbols.doc:
UnreachableSchedule is returned by Parse for a valid expression that
matches no date on the calendar, such as "0 0 30 2 *".

symbols.name: UnsupportedSyntax

code.public: That cron syntax is outside the accepted subset

symbols.doc:
UnsupportedSyntax is returned by Parse for a construct from another cron
dialect — a seconds field, @reboot, @every, L / W / # / ?.

symbols.name: Change
symbols.doc: Change is a stored transition, as an OnTransition hook receives it.

symbols.name: CodeDelayInvalid
symbols.doc:
CodeDelayInvalid identifies an After with a duration that is not positive
(0.3.88.17).

symbols.name: CodeEntityExists
symbols.doc:
CodeEntityExists identifies a Start whose entity's key the store already
holds (0.3.88.3).

symbols.name: CodeEntityMissing
symbols.doc:
CodeEntityMissing identifies a key the store holds no entity under — never
there, or deleted while a transition ran (0.3.88.2).

symbols.name: CodeEventInvalid
symbols.doc:
CodeEventInvalid identifies a transition declared with an empty event name,
or CreateEvent (0.3.88.15).

symbols.name: CodeFunctionMissing
symbols.doc:
CodeFunctionMissing identifies a nil accessor, guard, instant function, hook
or definition (0.3.88.18).

symbols.name: CodeFunctionPanicked
symbols.doc:
CodeFunctionPanicked identifies a guard or an instant function that panicked
(0.3.88.13).

symbols.name: CodeHookChangedKey
symbols.doc:
CodeHookChangedKey identifies an OnEnter hook that changed its entity's key
(0.3.88.8).

symbols.name: CodeHookChangedState
symbols.doc:
CodeHookChangedState identifies an OnEnter hook that changed the state it
was entering (0.3.88.7).

symbols.name: CodeHookFailed
symbols.doc: CodeHookFailed identifies a hook that returned an error (0.3.88.5).

symbols.name: CodeHookPanicked
symbols.doc:
CodeHookPanicked identifies a hook that panicked, recovered as an error
(0.3.88.6).

symbols.name: CodeInitialMissing
symbols.doc:
CodeInitialMissing identifies a definition with no initial state
(0.3.88.14).

symbols.name: CodeJournalFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeJournalFailed identifies a Journal method that returned an error
(0.3.88.11).

symbols.name: CodeKeyEmpty
symbols.doc:
CodeKeyEmpty identifies an entity handed to Start whose key is empty
(0.3.88.4).

symbols.name: CodeLoopPanicked
symbols.doc:
CodeLoopPanicked identifies a panic the loop recovered from a store, journal
or observer call (0.3.88.21).

symbols.name: CodeLoopRunning
symbols.doc:
CodeLoopRunning identifies a Run or a Step asked for while another is going
(0.3.88.12).

symbols.name: CodeReentrant
symbols.doc:
CodeReentrant identifies a Start or Fire through the context an OnEnter hook
of the same machine was given (0.3.88.9).

symbols.name: CodeStoreFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeStoreFailed identifies a Store method that returned an error
(0.3.88.10).

symbols.name: CodeStoreMissing
symbols.doc: CodeStoreMissing identifies a configuration with no store (0.3.88.19).

symbols.name: CodeTransitionDuplicate
symbols.doc:
CodeTransitionDuplicate identifies a second transition declared for one
event from one state (0.3.88.16).

symbols.name: CodeTransitionRefused
symbols.doc:
CodeTransitionRefused identifies an event no declared transition takes from
the entity's state (0.3.88.1).

symbols.name: CodeTriggerUnknown
symbols.doc: CodeTriggerUnknown identifies a name ParseTrigger does not know (0.2.56.1).

symbols.name: CodeWaitAbandoned
symbols.doc:
CodeWaitAbandoned identifies a caller whose context ended while the entity
was busy (0.3.88.20).

symbols.name: Config
symbols.doc: Config parameterises New. Only Store is required.

symbols.name: CreateEvent
symbols.doc:
CreateEvent is the event name of the step that brings a new entity into its
initial state; no declared transition may take it.
