symbols.name: DefaultMaxHistory
symbols.doc:
DefaultMaxHistory is how many transitions a Record keeps when
Config.MaxHistory is not positive.

symbols.name: DefaultMinGap
symbols.doc:
DefaultMinGap is the least time between two runs of the loop when
Config.MinGap is not positive.

symbols.name: Define
symbols.spelled: func[E any, S comparable](state func(*E) *S) *Definition[E, S]
symbols.canonical: func[E any, S comparable](state func(*E) *S) *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/statemachine.Definition[E, S]
symbols.doc:
Define starts the declaration of a machine over entities of type E. state
returns a pointer to the entity's state field.

symbols.name: Definition
symbols.doc: Definition declares a machine: its states, transitions and hooks.

symbols.name: DelayInvalid

code.public: A timer transition needs a positive duration

symbols.doc: DelayInvalid is an After with a duration that is not positive.

symbols.name: EntityExists

code.public: An entity with that key already exists

symbols.doc: EntityExists is returned by a Start over a key already taken (409).

symbols.name: EntityMissing

code.public: No such entity

symbols.doc:
EntityMissing is returned for a key the store holds no entity under, or one
deleted while the transition ran (404).

symbols.name: EventInvalid

code.public: A transition needs a name, other than the reserved one

symbols.doc:
EventInvalid is a transition declared with an empty event name, or
CreateEvent.

symbols.name: Firing
symbols.doc:
Firing is a transition the machine's own loop is about to fire, as
Config.Observe is told it.

symbols.name: FunctionMissing

code.public: The state machine was given no function where it needs one

symbols.doc:
FunctionMissing is a nil accessor, guard, instant function, hook or
definition.

symbols.name: FunctionPanicked

code.public: A state-machine guard or deadline function panicked

symbols.doc:
FunctionPanicked is a guard or an instant function that panicked; the entity
is retried after its backoff.

symbols.name: HookChangedKey

code.public: A state-machine hook changed the key of its entity

symbols.doc: HookChangedKey is an OnEnter hook that changed its entity's key.

symbols.name: HookChangedState

code.public: A state-machine hook changed the state it was entering

symbols.doc: HookChangedState is an OnEnter hook that changed the state it was entering.

symbols.name: HookFailed

code.public: A state-machine hook failed

symbols.doc: HookFailed accompanies a hook's own error, joined beside it.

symbols.name: HookPanicked

code.public: A state-machine hook panicked

symbols.doc:
HookPanicked is a hook that panicked and was recovered; the value and the
stack are log-only fields.

symbols.name: InitialMissing

code.public: The state machine has no initial state

symbols.doc:
InitialMissing is returned by New for a definition that never called
Initial.

symbols.name: Journal
symbols.doc:
Journal is the port the machine keeps its records in, beside your store.
It is frozen at three methods.

symbols.name: JournalFailed

code.public: The state machine's journal failed

symbols.doc: JournalFailed wraps an error a Journal method returned.

symbols.name: KeyEmpty

code.public: The entity has no key

symbols.doc: KeyEmpty is returned by a Start with an entity whose key is empty.

symbols.name: LoopEvent
symbols.doc: LoopEvent is what Config.OnLoop is told about Run.

symbols.name: LoopEventKind
symbols.doc: LoopEventKind says what a LoopEvent reports.

symbols.name: LoopPanicked

code.public: The state machine's loop recovered a panic

symbols.doc:
LoopPanicked is a panic the loop recovered from a store, journal or observer
call: the entity is retried after its backoff, unless it came from the
observer's end, once the transition was stored.

symbols.name: LoopRunEnded
symbols.doc: LoopRunEnded reports a run ending: every field is set.

symbols.name: LoopRunStarted
symbols.doc: LoopRunStarted reports a run starting: Wake and Started are set.

symbols.name: LoopRunning

code.public: The state machine's loop is already running

symbols.doc: LoopRunning is returned by Run or Step while another is going.

symbols.name: LoopWaiting
symbols.doc:
LoopWaiting reports the loop re-armed to wake earlier, at Next, because a
write arrived while it slept.

symbols.name: Machine
symbols.doc: Machine runs a Definition over a Store. It is safe for concurrent use.

symbols.name: New
symbols.spelled: func[E any, S comparable](ctx context.Context, def *Definition[E, S], cfg *Config[E, S]) (*Machine[E, S], error)
symbols.canonical: func[E any, S comparable](ctx context.Context, def *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/statemachine.Definition[E, S], cfg *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/statemachine.Config[E, S]) (*github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/statemachine.Machine[E, S], error)
symbols.doc:
New checks def and cfg and opens a machine over cfg.Store: it reads the
journal and every entity once, reconciles them and schedules what is due.
Every problem of the declaration is returned at once, joined.

symbols.name: ParseTrigger
symbols.doc:
ParseTrigger reads a trigger's name — "start", "event", "delay", "deadline"
or "guard" — as Trigger.String writes it.

symbols.name: Record
symbols.doc:
Record is what the machine keeps about one entity: its state, since when,
and its latest transitions.

symbols.name: Reentrant

code.public: A state-machine hook cannot fire its own machine

symbols.doc:
Reentrant is a Start or Fire through the context an OnEnter hook of the same
machine was given: refused, not deadlocked.

symbols.name: Step
symbols.doc: Step is one transition in a Record's history.

symbols.name: Store
symbols.doc:
Store is the port your entities are read and written through. It is frozen
at five methods.

symbols.name: StoreFailed

code.public: The state machine's store failed

symbols.doc: StoreFailed wraps an error a Store method returned.

symbols.name: StoreMissing

code.public: The state machine has no store

symbols.doc: StoreMissing is returned by New when Config.Store is nil.

symbols.name: Transition
symbols.doc: Transition is a declared transition, as Definition.Transitions reads it back.

symbols.name: TransitionDuplicate

code.public: That event already leaves that state

symbols.doc: TransitionDuplicate is one event declared twice from one state.

symbols.name: TransitionRefused

code.public: That transition is not possible from the current state

symbols.doc:
TransitionRefused is returned when no transition by that event leaves the
entity's state (409); the entity comes back with it.

symbols.name: Trigger
symbols.doc:
Trigger says what fired a transition: a start, an event, a delay, a
deadline or a guard.

symbols.name: TriggerDeadline
symbols.doc:
TriggerDeadline is the arrival of an instant the entity carries
(Definition.At).

symbols.name: TriggerDelay
symbols.doc: TriggerDelay is a duration the entity spent in its state (Definition.After).

symbols.name: TriggerEvent
symbols.doc: TriggerEvent is an event a caller fired.

symbols.name: TriggerGuard
symbols.doc:
TriggerGuard is a guard on the entity that held after a write
(Definition.When).

symbols.name: TriggerStart
symbols.doc: TriggerStart is a Start: the entity entered its initial state.

symbols.name: TriggerUnknown

code.public: That is not a state-machine trigger

symbols.doc: TriggerUnknown refuses a trigger name outside the five.

symbols.name: WaitAbandoned

code.public: The request ended while the entity was busy

symbols.doc:
WaitAbandoned is returned when the context ended while the entity was busy
(503); errors.Is still finds the context's error.

symbols.name: Wake
symbols.doc: Wake says why a run of the loop started.

symbols.name: WakeChange
symbols.doc: WakeChange is a run a write woke the loop for.

symbols.name: WakeDue
symbols.doc: WakeDue is a run the loop woke for by itself: a transition fell due.

symbols.name: WakeStart
symbols.doc: WakeStart is the first run, when Run starts.

symbols.name: All
symbols.doc:
All runs every constraint and reports everything they found. It is the
default shape of the engine; All with no constraint accepts everything.

symbols.name: AtLeast
symbols.doc:
AtLeast refuses a value below lo; the bound is inclusive. It is the
programmatic spelling of the `min=` struct tag, and both report the rule
"min".

symbols.name: AtMost
symbols.doc:
AtMost refuses a value above hi; the bound is inclusive. It is the
programmatic spelling of the `max=` struct tag.

symbols.name: Between
symbols.spelled: func[T cmp.Ordered](lo T, hi T) (constraint Constraint[T], err error)
symbols.canonical: func[T cmp.Ordered](lo T, hi T) (constraint github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/validation.Constraint[T], err error)
symbols.doc:
Between refuses a value outside [lo, hi]. lo > hi is refused at
construction: an inverted interval is satisfied by nothing.

symbols.name: Check
symbols.doc:
Check runs constraints against value at the root path and converts the
result to the SDK error model — the one-line bridge to config.Validator.

symbols.name: CodeLengthOutOfRange
symbols.doc: CodeLengthOutOfRange identifies a size outside its bounds.

symbols.name: CodeNotInSet
symbols.doc: CodeNotInSet identifies a value outside its allowed set.

symbols.name: CodeOutOfRange
symbols.doc: CodeOutOfRange identifies an ordered value outside its bounds.

symbols.name: CodePatternMismatch
symbols.doc: CodePatternMismatch identifies a string that did not match its pattern.

symbols.name: CodeRequired
symbols.doc: CodeRequired identifies an absent value.

symbols.name: Constraint
symbols.doc:
Constraint is the public alias for the value-checking port. It is a FUNC
type, so it cannot grow a method and break a downstream implementer
(ADR 0039).

symbols.name: Count
symbols.spelled: func[E any](minLen int, maxLen int) (constraint Constraint[[]E], err error)
symbols.canonical: func[E any](minLen int, maxLen int) (constraint github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/validation.Constraint[[]E], err error)
symbols.doc:
Count refuses a slice whose element count falls outside [min, max]. max may
be [Unbounded]. Count(1, Unbounded) is how presence is expressed for a slice.

symbols.name: Each
symbols.spelled: func[T, E any](name string, get func(T) []E, constraints ...Constraint[E]) (constraint Constraint[T], err error)
symbols.canonical: func[T, E any](name string, get func(T) []E, constraints ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/validation.Constraint[E]) (constraint github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/validation.Constraint[T], err error)
symbols.doc:
Each applies constraints to every element of a slice member of T reached
through get, locating each element's violations at "name[i]".

symbols.name: Failed

code.public: One or more values did not satisfy their constraints

symbols.doc:
Failed is the error a non-empty Report converts to. Its HTTP status is
422: the request was syntactically fine and semantically wrong, which is
what a failed validation is — not a 500.

symbols.name: Field
symbols.spelled: func[T, F any](name string, get func(T) F, constraints ...Constraint[F]) (constraint Constraint[T], err error)
symbols.canonical: func[T, F any](name string, get func(T) F, constraints ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/validation.Constraint[F]) (constraint github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/validation.Constraint[T], err error)
symbols.doc:
Field applies constraints to a member of T reached through get, locating
every violation at the parent path extended by name. It uses no reflection.

symbols.name: First
symbols.doc:
First runs the constraints in order and stops at the one that refuses. It is
a real short-circuit, not a filtered report.

symbols.name: InvalidRule

code.public: The validate struct tag could not be compiled

symbols.doc: InvalidRule is returned by Struct when a validate tag cannot be compiled.

symbols.name: JoinField
symbols.doc:
JoinField extends a path with a member name — JoinField("user", "zip") is
"user.zip". The grammar does not quote, so a member name that itself
contains '.', '[' or ']' yields a path indistinguishable from a nested or
indexed one.

symbols.name: JoinIndex
symbols.doc:
JoinIndex extends a path with an element position — JoinIndex("a", 2) is
"a[2]".

symbols.name: Length
symbols.spelled: func(minRunes int, maxRunes int) (constraint Constraint[string], err error)
symbols.canonical: func(minRunes int, maxRunes int) (constraint github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/validation.Constraint[string], err error)
symbols.doc:
Length refuses a string whose RUNE count falls outside [min, max]. max may
be [Unbounded]. It counts runes, not grapheme clusters.

symbols.name: Matches
symbols.doc:
Matches refuses a string the pattern does not match. The pattern is compiled
at construction, and Go's RE2 has no backtracking — a pattern cannot be
turned into a denial of service by the value it is shown.

symbols.name: Misconfigured

code.public: The constraint cannot be built from the given configuration

symbols.doc:
Misconfigured is returned by a constraint CONSTRUCTOR whose arguments it
cannot honour — an inverted interval, an empty set, a bad pattern.

symbols.name: Must
symbols.spelled: func[T any](constraint Constraint[T], err error) Constraint[T]
symbols.doc:
Must returns constraint, panicking when err is non-nil. It is the
regexp.MustCompile idiom, for a package-level validator built from literals
at init. Do NOT use it on a bound that comes from configuration.

symbols.name: OneOf
symbols.doc:
OneOf refuses a value absent from allowed. An empty allowed set is refused
at construction: it is a forgotten argument, not a permissive rule.

symbols.name: Report
symbols.doc:
Report is the public alias for everything one validation found wrong. Its
zero value — nil — is a passing report.

symbols.name: Required
symbols.doc:
Required refuses the zero value of T. It cannot distinguish "not supplied"
from "supplied as zero" — declare the field as a pointer when that matters.

symbols.name: RootPath
symbols.doc:
RootPath is the path of the value handed to a validator, before any
descent. A violation reported there is about the value as a whole.

symbols.name: Struct
symbols.spelled: func[T any](cfg StructConfig) (constraint Constraint[T], err error)
symbols.doc:
Struct compiles the `validate` tags of T into a Constraint, caching the plan
per (type, mode).

Accepted: required, min, max, minlen, maxlen, mincount, maxcount,
oneof=a|b|c, dive. Refused BY NAME, each saying what to do instead: pattern
/ regex (a regexp cannot live in a comma-separated tag), email, url, uuid,
dive into a map, and any unknown rule.

symbols.name: StructConfig
symbols.doc: StructConfig is the public alias for a compiled struct validator's options.

symbols.name: Unbounded
symbols.doc: Unbounded is the [Length] / [Count] upper bound that means "no ceiling".

symbols.name: UnsupportedTarget

code.public: Struct tag validation requires a struct type

symbols.doc: UnsupportedTarget is returned by Struct when T is not a struct type.

symbols.name: Violation
symbols.doc: Violation is the public alias for one located failure.

symbols.name: Available
symbols.doc:
Available returns every registered [Engine], sorted, so a program can print
what its imports actually wired up.

symbols.name: Config
symbols.doc:
Config parameterises every engine. FS is required; everything else has a
defensible default.

symbols.name: ContentTypeHTML
symbols.doc:
ContentTypeHTML is the media type an HTML [Renderer] reports, charset
included — a response with no charset is sniffed, and a document sniffed
as UTF-7 can smuggle markup past an escaper that judged the bytes as
UTF-8.

symbols.name: DefaultMaxBytes
symbols.doc:
DefaultMaxBytes is the ceiling [Config].MaxBytes clamps to when it is not
positive: 8 MiB. There is deliberately no spelling for "unlimited".

symbols.name: DuplicateEngine

code.public: Two view engines claim the same name

symbols.doc:
DuplicateEngine is the boot-time panic for two distinct factories under
one Engine name. It is refused rather than resolved, because one of the
two would silently decide how every value in the program is escaped.

symbols.name: Engine
symbols.doc:
Engine names a registered template engine. The zero value is the reserved
invalid name.

symbols.name: EngineInvalid

code.public: The view engine registration is not usable

symbols.doc:
EngineInvalid is the boot-time panic for a nil Factory or one claiming
the empty Engine name.

symbols.name: EngineUnknown

code.public: No view engine is registered under that name

symbols.doc:
EngineUnknown is returned by [Open] for a name no factory claims —
usually an engine package that was never imported.

symbols.name: Factory
symbols.doc:
Factory is the plug-in contract an engine implements to enter the registry.
Registering is a promise the security model rests on — see [Register].

symbols.name: HTML
symbols.doc:
HTML is the [Engine] name of the stdlib html/template implementation. It
is the only engine the SDK ships.

symbols.name: New
symbols.doc:
New builds the stdlib html/template [Renderer] over cfg.FS, parsing the
whole tree eagerly.

Call it once, at start-up, and keep the result: see the package
documentation's parse-once rule. A nil FS, a file that does not parse and a
template whose escaping context cannot be resolved are all refused here, so
a broken tree is a deploy that does not come up.

An EMPTY tree is not an error. It produces a Renderer that refuses every
name with [TemplateNotFound] — loud rather than inert (ADR 0031).

symbols.name: Open
symbols.spelled: func(name Engine, cfg Config) (renderer Renderer, err error)
symbols.doc:
Open resolves an [Engine] by name and builds a [Renderer] from cfg. It is
the configuration-driven counterpart to [New].

It fails loudly on a name nobody claims — [EngineUnknown] — rather than
falling back to a default, because a fallback here would let a typo in a
configuration file silently choose how every value in the program is
escaped.

symbols.name: Register
symbols.doc:
Register inserts f under f.Engine() and returns it, so a third-party engine
can bind the singleton to a package-level variable.

Registration is not merely a name binding. An engine in this registry MUST
contextually escape every value it renders for the media type its
ContentType reports, render into its own buffer and return complete bytes or
none, honour Config.MaxBytes, refuse at construction a Config it cannot
honour, and name every template by its slash path within Config.FS.

It panics on a nil factory, on the empty [Engine] name, and when a DISTINCT
factory already claims the name — at import, where the offender is visible.

symbols.name: RenderFailed

code.public: The page could not be rendered

symbols.doc:
RenderFailed is returned when execution started and could not finish.
Nothing is returned alongside it: the partial bytes are discarded
inside the engine.

symbols.name: RenderTooLarge

code.public: The page could not be rendered

symbols.doc:
RenderTooLarge is returned when a render reached Config.MaxBytes. It is
a denial-of-service guard, not a formatting complaint.

symbols.name: Renderer
symbols.doc:
Renderer turns a named template and a data value into a complete document:
Render and ContentType.

The method set is FROZEN at two. New capabilities arrive as SIBLING
interfaces reached by type assertion, because this alias publishes the
interface, Go interfaces are structural, and a third method would break
every downstream implementer at compile time with no deprecation window
(ADR 0039).

symbols.name: TemplateNotFound

code.public: The requested view does not exist

symbols.doc:
TemplateNotFound is returned by Render for a name the engine does not
hold, including the empty name. A Renderer over an empty tree is
legitimate and refuses everything by name.

symbols.name: TemplateParseFailed

code.public: A view template is not valid

symbols.doc:
TemplateParseFailed is returned for a file html/template refused to
parse or could not build an escaping plan for.

symbols.name: TemplateSourceFailed

code.public: The view templates could not be read

symbols.doc:
TemplateSourceFailed is returned when the template FS could not be READ
— usually an embed pattern that matched nothing.

symbols.name: TrustHTML
symbols.doc:
TrustHTML marks s as HTML that is already safe to write unescaped.

It is the one bypass the SDK offers and the only spelling it has, so "where
does this codebase decide to trust markup?" is one grep with one answer.
Read the package documentation before using it: the SDK cannot verify the
assertion this call makes.

symbols.name: TrustedHTML
symbols.doc:
TrustedHTML is an HTML fragment written WITHOUT escaping.

It is an ALIAS of html/template.HTML, and that has a consequence stated
rather than hidden: the engine cannot tell a fragment marked through
[TrustHTML] from one a caller converted directly. See the package
documentation.

symbols.name: UnsafeValue

code.public: The page could not be rendered

symbols.doc:
UnsafeValue is returned when render data carries one of the six refused
html/template trust types. The fields name the path and the type, never
the value.

symbols.name: ViewMisconfigured

code.public: The view renderer cannot be built from the given configuration

symbols.doc:
ViewMisconfigured is returned by a constructor for a Config it cannot
honour: a nil FS, a tree that does not parse, or a template
html/template cannot contextually escape.
